title: Deferred reservation proxy + shortburst-gating SLO sentinel
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally hit transient short-duration demand spikes that cannot be satisfied by the normal reservation allocator without over-provisioning. Large allocations for these very short events pump cost and destabilize fairness. This PR introduces a deferred reservation proxy layer that accepts short-duration admission requests, settles reservations asynchronously against the main ledger, and exposes a lightweight gating signal (shortburst-gate) that upstream routers and admission controllers can consult to make fast local decisions. Design: 1) deferred_proxy component runs as an independent actor in the autoscaler with a small memory-only ledger for tentative admits; it uses optimistic admission and then attempts to commit to the primary reservation store with bounded retries. 2) shortburst-gate signal summarizes recent tentative admit density, commit success ratio, and time-to-commit distribution; it is emitted at 5s granularity. 3) a sentinel reporter aggregates gate metrics into the observability stack and triggers an SLO degradation alert if commit-ratio<80% for a sustained window. 4) a feature flag (dedicated.deferred_proxy.enabled) controls rollout and a safe-mode path falls back to immediate reservation semantics. Implementation notes: added circuit-breaker to limit concurrency against reservation store, exponential backoff on commits, and strict idempotency keys to avoid double-commit. API: no user-facing API changes; config knobs in configs/dedicated/defaults.yaml and operator-facing flags for rollout. Tests: unit tests for optimistic admit logic, integration test that simulates commit contention and verifies fallback. Deployment: staged rollout behind feature flag, start with 5% of fleets for 48h then 25% then 100% if metrics stable. Related work: builds on prior autoscaler improvements (ENG-4210) but focuses on ephemeral admission smoothing rather than long-term credits.

release_notes: Adds a deferred reservation proxy and shortburst gating signal to allow lightweight, optimistic admission for short-lived demand spikes. Helps reduce over-provisioning and smooth transient surges while preserving fairness. Rollout behind feature flag; requires no customer API change.
test_plan: Unit tests added for commit idempotency, concurrency ceilings, and backoff. Integration sim reproduces commit contention and validates fallback to immediate reservation. E2E fixture exercises the feature flag path. Manual canary: enable on small fleet subset, validate commit_success_ratio>90% and queue latency impact <10ms p95 before scaling rollout.
performance_results: Synthetic load test against a 200-node dedicated fleet: with deferred proxy enabled p50 admission latency unchanged, p95 admission latency increased by 4ms on accepted path, overall reservation store QPS reduced by ~18%, and measured cost simulations show ~3.5% lower transient allocation cost during bursty workloads. Short-term tail instability observed when commit_ratio dropped below 60% which triggered sentinel and immediate fallback; this was addressed by lowering commit concurrency and adding backoff.
notes: No breaking changes. Feature behind flag. Operators should monitor dedicated.deferred_proxy.commit_success_ratio and dedicated.shortburst.gate_open_ratio during rollout.
